prompt.context: Our client, WhistleTips, is an R&D firm located in the United States who has recently patented a semi truck spoiler technology that reduces air resistance for semi trucks of all types. When installed, the spoiler improves fuel efficiency by 25%. WhistleTips has no experience in the trucking or automotive industry, but they believe that this is a game changing product and want to enter the market.
prompt.question: WhistleTips has asked us for help to identify how they should enter this market and sell their product. How should they approach market entry and how should they price their spoiler?

clarifying_info.q: What does the spoiler actually do for the truck?
clarifying_info.a: The wings are useful because they improve a semi truck's MPG by reducing air resistance.

clarifying_info.q: Does WhistleTips have any manufacturing, distribution, or sales strategies in place?
clarifying_info.a: WhistleTips has not yet developed specific manufacturing, distribution, or sales strategies.

exhibits.title: Relative Frequency of Driving Speeds
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of time semi trucks spend driving at each speed range: <25 mph, 25-50 mph, 50-75 mph, and >75 mph.

exhibits.title: MPG for Each Speed Range
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the miles per gallon (MPG) a semi truck achieves at each speed range: <25 mph, 25-50 mph, 50-75 mph, and >75 mph.

framework: Market entry strategy: evaluate manufacturing options (own facility vs. contract manufacturing) and production style (made-to-order vs. large batch)
Distribution strategy: physical storefront, online, partnership with semi truck retailers, wholesale to trucking companies, outreach to independent drivers
Market sizing and penetration: understand the size of the U.S. semi truck market and realistic adoption rate
Quantify value delivered: calculate weighted average MPG improvement and total savings per truck over useful life
Pricing analysis: set price to cover COGS, SG&A, and recoup R&D within target timeframe while remaining below total value delivered to customer
Risk assessment: competition, brand recognition, patent protection, gas price volatility, and willingness of industry to adopt new technology

questions.prompt: Question 1: In what ways could WhistleTips enter the market, both on a manufacturing and distribution basis?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify multiple manufacturing and distribution options and discuss benefits and risks of each. Strong answers will proactively ask what additional information would help make the decision (initial investment costs, market size, patent protection outside the U.S., potential competitors, industry willingness to adopt, industry fragmentation).

questions.prompt: Question 2: Our client has provided truck driving statistics (Exhibits 1 and 2). How many more miles (on average) will the truck travel per gallon with the spoiler installed?
questions.guidance: Candidate must read both charts to extract MPG and time-distribution by speed band, compute a weighted average baseline MPG, then apply the 25% efficiency improvement from the prompt. Final answer: the truck travels 3 more miles per gallon with the spoiler installed.

math.setup: Weighted average baseline MPG = sum of (MPG_i * time_share_i) across all speed bands. Then apply 25% improvement.
math.answer: 3 additional miles per gallon with the spoiler installed

questions.prompt: Question 4 (labeled as Q4 in casebook): What is the total savings per truck by installing the spoiler?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask for miles driven per year, cost per gallon, and expected useful life of the wing. They then calculate gallons saved per year and multiply by fuel cost and lifespan. Answer: $3,900 total savings per truck over the spoiler's useful life.

math.setup: Use baseline 12 MPG and improved 15 MPG, miles driven per year, fuel cost, and useful life. (Provide when asked: 18,000 miles/year, $2.60/gallon, 5-year useful life.)
steps: Total gallons used per year without spoiler = 18,000 / 12 = 1,500 gallons
Total gallons used per year with spoiler = 18,000 / 15 = 1,200 gallons
math.answer: $3,900 total savings per truck over the spoiler's 5-year useful life

questions.prompt: Question 5: WhistleTips has decided to use a contracted manufacturer and wants to recoup R&D costs in the first year. Based on a market size of 20,000 semi trucks in the United States, how would you suggest WhistleTips price the spoiler? What concerns do you have about this price?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify costs (COGS + SG&A), assume a market penetration rate (20% = 4,000 trucks is the reference assumption, but must be justified), calculate required contribution per unit to cover R&D, then derive minimum price. They should also reason about pricing between $3,000 and $3,900 and articulate risks. Strong candidates note that time value of money makes the $3,900 ceiling less attractive to buyers, and discuss concerns about penetration achievability, lack of brand/sales team, competition, and gas price variability.

math.setup: Provide when asked: R&D cost = $8,000,000; COGS = $900/unit; SG&A = $100/unit (total cost = $1,000/unit); assume 20% market penetration = 4,000 trucks.
steps: Required contribution per unit to cover R&D = $8,000,000 / 4,000 = $2,000
Maximum defensible price = total savings delivered = $3,900
math.answer: Minimum price = $3,000; suggested range $3,000-$3,900; candidate should pick a specific price and justify it

brainstorming.prompt: What additional information would help WhistleTips make better market entry and pricing decisions?

categories.name: Market & Competitive Landscape
ideas: Size of the addressable market (number of semi trucks in the U.S.)
Patent protection outside the United States
Industry fragmentation (many small fleets vs. a few large carriers)

categories.name: Customer & Adoption
ideas: Willingness of the trucking industry to adopt the new technology
Decision-maker within trucking companies (fleet managers vs. owner-operators)
Time to payback expected by buyers
Current awareness of fuel efficiency solutions

categories.name: Financial & Operational
ideas: Initial investment costs for own manufacturing vs. contract manufacturing
Quality control risks with contract manufacturing
Sales and distribution partnership terms with current semi truck retailers
Impact of fuel price volatility on value proposition

recommendation: WhistleTips should enter via a contracted manufacturer to avoid large upfront capital expenditure for its own plant, and distribute through partnerships with existing semi truck retailers and direct outreach to large trucking fleets.

Price the spoiler at approximately $3,000-$3,500 to recoup R&D costs within the first year at a 20% penetration rate, while still delivering clear savings to customers relative to the $3,900 total value over the spoiler's useful life.
risks: 20% market penetration may be optimistic given WhistleTips has no brand recognition or established sales force in the trucking industry.
Competition from new entrants or incumbents could undercut pricing after the product launches.
The fuel savings value proposition is sensitive to gas prices; if prices fall, the ROI to truckers shrinks and demand may decline.
Delayed realization of savings (spread over 5 years) reduces buyer willingness to pay a high upfront price due to time value of money.
Patent protection may not extend outside the U.S., limiting global market opportunity.
next_steps: Conduct detailed market research on fleet owner purchasing behavior and willingness to pay.
Identify and negotiate with 2-3 major semi truck retailer or fleet partners to establish distribution.
Model multiple penetration scenarios (10%, 20%, 30%) and stress-test pricing against gas price assumptions.
Assess patent filing status in key international markets (Canada, EU, Mexico) to protect future expansion.
